chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hammad from Sadeer from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

On the Day of Resurrection, a group of people will be raised under the shade of the Throne, their faces from light, their garments from light, sitting on chairs of light. He said: The creatures will honor them, saying, 'These are the prophets.' A caller will cry out from under the Throne, 'No, these are not prophets.' He said: They will say, 'These are the martyrs.' The caller will cry out from under the Throne, 'No, these are not martyrs, but these are a people who made it easy for the believers and granted time to the insolvent debtor until he became capable (of repayment).'

key_terms.تَحْتَ ظِلِّ الْعَرْشِ: Under the shade of the Throne
key_terms.یُیَسِّرُونَ: They made it easy / granted leniency

ai.seo_question: Who are the people sitting under the Throne on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this unique honor in *Thawab al-A'mal*, distinguishing these individuals from prophets and martyrs to emphasize the spiritual weight of financial mercy in Shia tradition. Their status under the Throne signifies that easing the burden of the indebted is a form of worship that secures divine proximity, reflecting the practical application of *mu'amalat* (transactions) as a path to salvation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Abdillah b. Ja’far al-Himyari from Ya’qub b. Yazid from al-Hassan b. Mahbub from Hamad from Sadeer from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

“Some people would be sitting on the chairs of light under the shade of the Divine Throne having bright faces and wearing illuminated dresses. People will wonder, ‘Are they prophets?’ A caller would say, ‘No’. People will ask, ‘Are they martyrs?’ The caller would reply, ‘They are not martyrs. They used to remain lenient with the believers and used to give time to debtors to repay loans and used to ask them to repay the loan whenever they are capable of it’.”
